limitations: Downloader, metadata and commit results are explicitly controlled; no network, storage durability, audio or physical Android claim. Production archive-browser.js owns full-source integration.

Fault injections are explicit: one interrupted audio request, one deferred request cancelled by the production API, one native stage-store put throwing QuotaExceededError and one same-length corrupted network body. Native stage corruption is performed only in this disposable IndexedDB database.

The shared browser fixture deliberately blocks external requests; those observations remain in externalBlocked. Unexpected-request assertions and exact served-file proofs cover the application origin.

Disposable Linux Chromium and local HTTP transport. All291 original archive payloads are downloaded and rehashed; this is bounded scale acceptance, not a mobile-bandwidth, speed, memory, quota or performance claim.

Chromium may report a completed WebM fetch as ERR_ABORTED. Such observations are accepted only with a unique original same-origin URL, HTTP200, native response-end timing, native staged-Blob SHA/size and matching disk/served receipts. Unknown, incomplete or corrupt request failures remain failures.

The only policy substitution reports unlocked:true so berhet/mzbz records join the full archive. It is not PIN verification, membership authorization or a privacy-security test. Production download, preview, commit, native storage and application source bytes are unchanged.

An old generic-bank WAV and a separate personal WAV are labelled fixture sentinels; no real user recording/profile is read. Disposable native Chromium context with an actual installed service worker and complete verified release graph. Classic/Feyz; no physical Android, screen lock or audible-quality claim.
Only the four original temel WebM files187655 bytes are staged. The suite does not claim that all291 optional recordings were downloaded.

One worker-owned original audio network request is deliberately aborted to create a durable partial stage. Browser context routes observe real worker requests; the source service worker and downloader remain unchanged.

CacheStorage is enumerated across every cache before/after each archive lifecycle. The offline socket gate plus context offline emulation explicitly prevent the worker from obtaining live optional bytes through a fallback.

Worker-owned ERR_ABORTED observations are retained separately when their exact required-runtime or optional-art URL has independently verified current cached bytes matching pinned local and served digests. This proves artifact readiness, not successful completion of those aborted requests; their cause is not established. Separate deliberate offline-denial observations require exact worker IDs, the cold-reload gate phase, known shell/marker/art URLs and fresh cached bytes; EMPTY_RESPONSE also requires an actual socket-denial receipt. Unknown URLs, page-owned aborts, other unexpected codes and all unplanned archive-stage failures remain blocking.
